top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a distinct invention: a magic-wavelength trap cancels the light shift while many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime, giving ensemble statistics and systematic control together. It is independently reproduced and intercompared at the 1e-18 level across several national laboratories and has already produced new physics (mm-scale gravitational redshift, constants and dark-matter bounds, many-body clocks). The two-name split by contribution type is compact and defensible, and a stand-alone prize avoids a second part with no common thread. P002 adds Hosono, a mature and cleanly credited discovery that I rank above no award but defer to colleagues on; no award is the weakest outcome given such a mature candidate.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no personal tie to Katori, Ye or Hosono, though as WACQT director and a metrology-adjacent quantum physicist I note only general field proximity to precision quantum measurement
